messages:
julia-cust: Customer on private VPC reported sudden 429s and intermittent 401s after our last runtime deploy. Spike started ~2026-03-12T09:15:00Z. They say requests get "rate_limited" and sometimes "auth_error". EU region, customer-managed gateway in k8s. Any quick triage steps?
alex-support: can you paste the gateway pod logs? short excerpt is fine. also which ingress (nginx/contour/envoy)?
mike-sre: tagging in — likely token-bucket overflow at the gateway or the ingress controller dropping when burst window exceeded. Also possible auth proxy (kong/authz) timing out under burst so we see 401.
julia-cust: ingress is envoy via our distro, pods: gateway-0..2, envoy version 1.25. Shipped last night. logs: ```2026-03-12T09:15:07Z ERROR http request failed status=429 path=/v1/generate err="rate_limited" remote=10.0.2.14``` and ```2026-03-12T09:15:12Z WARN auth proxy timeout user=svc-account request_id=abc123 status=401```.
alex-support: perfect — can you run `kubectl -n customer get pods -l app=gateway -o wide` and `kubectl -n customer exec -it gateway-0 -- envoy stats | grep ratelimit`?
mike-sre: typical thing: ingress has a token_bucket config: `tokens_per_sec`, `max_burst_tokens`. If `max_burst_tokens` too small,  bursts from client (e.g., fanout from many clients) will be rejected before upstream sees them. Also if auth proxy is synchronous, backpressure causes auth to fail with 401/timeout.
julia-cust: ran commands, output small bits: ```gateway-0  Ready  2/2  44m 10.0.2.14``` and envoy stats snippet: ```ratelimit_service.over_limit: 173
http.ingress_response.429: 168
cluster.auth_proxy.upstream_rq_4xx: 45```
nina-billing: note — rejected 429s are not billed for token usage; but customer called out billing spike earlier today which seems separate. We'll keep that note.
alex-support: ok repro hypothesis: burst pattern -> envoy token bucket exhausted -> 429. the 401s likely from auth proxy timeouts due to increased retries/backoff. Steps to confirm: 1) capture pcap or tcpdump at gateway to see burst patterns; 2) check envoy `token_bucket` config in ConfigMap or CRD; 3) verify auth-proxy latency under load.
mike-sre: commands: ```# check token bucket config in configmap
kubectl -n customer get configmap gateway-config -o yaml | sed -n '/token_bucket/,/max_burst/p'
# check envoy runtime values
kubectl -n customer exec gateway-0 -- curl -s localhost:9901/runtime?format=json | jq '.ratelimit'```
julia-cust: found config: `token_bucket: { tokens_per_sec: 50, max_burst_tokens: 100 }`. Traffic at spike measured ~800 requests/sec aggregated across 3 pods (~266 rps/pod) with many short spikes.
mike-sre: ah — tokens_per_sec 50 * 3 pods = 150/s sustained but bursts exceed. max_burst_tokens 100 per pod only buys ~2s of headroom. Solution options: - increase `max_burst_tokens` to 1000 or so; - enable prefix caching/KV cache at runtime to reduce downstream auth calls; - add local leaky buffer (sidecar) or configure envoy rate limiter to use global store (redis) for shared token bucket across pods.
alex-support: short-term hotfix: bump `max_burst_tokens` on ConfigMap and roll gateway pods. sample patch: ```apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  token_bucket: |
    tokens_per_sec: 50
    max_burst_tokens: 1200``` then `kubectl -n customer apply -f cm.yaml && kubectl -n customer rollout restart deploy/gateway`.
julia-cust: can we avoid billing surprises if we change this? customer worried we'll start charging for retries.
 nina-billing: we won't retro-bill. Post-fix: normal billing resumes. recommend capturing a snapshot of rejected vs accepted counts for audit.
mike-sre: follow-ups: - verify `auth-proxy` has connection pool size > burst concurrency, or make it async. - consider increasing ingress `burst` annotation (if using nginx) e.g., `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections` / `limit-rpm` equivalents. For envoy, use `upstream_flow_control` adjustments.
julia-cust: we rolled `max_burst_tokens` to 1200 and restarted deployment at 09:40. 10 minutes in, 429 rate dropped to single digits, auth timeouts gone. customer still wants write-up and repro steps.
alex-support: doc snippet for postmortem: - symptom: 429 + 401 after deploy - cause: token_bucket max_burst too low for customer traffic shape (high short spikes) + auth-proxy sync causing timeouts - mitigation: increase max_burst_tokens, enable KV cache for prefix hits, scale out gateway replicas or use shared rate limiter backend - next actions: add a runbook checklist + automated alert on http.ingress_response.429 p99 > threshold.
mike-sre: repro steps we used: ```1) k6 test with 800 concurrent VUs hitting /v1/generate with short sleeps (0-10ms) to simulate bursty fanout
2) observe envoy stats: http.ingress_response.429 and ratelimit_service.over_limit
3) run with old config, then patch cm to new max_burst_tokens and observe drop in 429s```
nina-billing: added billing note to ticket. recommending that we mark the incident as "no-cost" for the customer and generate usage CSV for their audit.
julia-cust: thanks all. leaving the ticket open for one business day to confirm no regression. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployment gateway v2.1.4 rolled at 2026-03-12T09:40:22Z by ops (restart triggered).
